targets.authors: Glassenberg, A. N., Feinberg, D. R., Jones, B. C., Little, A. C., & DeBruine, L. M.
targets.title: Sex-dimorphic face shape preference in heterosexual and homosexual men and women
targets.evidence_quote: Because results from other types of tests of the proposal that women adjust their mate preferences according to the probability of reproduction do not appear to be reliable (e.g., Jones et al., 2018; Marcinkowska et al., 2018, 2019; Zietsch et al., 2015), we undertook a direct replication of Glassenberg et al’s (2010) comparison of heterosexual and homosexual women’s preferences for masculinized versus feminized versions of male and female faces.
targets.outcome_quote: We found that heterosexual women demonstrated stronger preferences for masculinized male faces than did homosexual women. This relationship between sexual orientation and women’s masculinity preferences directly replicates the results reported by Glassenberg et al. (2010).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly report direct replication of the original male-face result and also directly replicate the female-face result. Batres et al. is corroborating context, not the study this paper sets out to re-test.
